Yup, this is what I argued the moment I saw the play.

I don't think it was a catch under the rules because he was already going to the ground when his feet came to the ground and under the rules if you're going to the ground in the process of making a catch, you have to maintain possession of the ball all the way to the ground (without the ball hitting the ground/or you going out of bounds). He did not maintain possession of the ball through the process of going to the ground and the ball came loose when it hit the ground. No catch.

Here's the conundrum for me. I feel like that SHOULD have been a catch under the rules, even though the rules state that shouldn't have been a catch.

However I feel like the rules should be as objective as possible and virtually any rule change that would allow that to be a catch would only make the rule more subjective. When calls become more subjective, they also become enforced in a much less uniform manner and that's bad for football.
